messages.subject: sliding landmarks on centerline
parts:
Hi everyone,

I was hoping someone in this group could give me a software recommendation. I have been using geomorph to analyse some 3D landmark data that I have digitised using Amira. To do this, I created centerlines (skeletonization) of my 3D shapes and placed the landmarks on there. I understand geomorph has the option to digitise landmarks and sliding landmarks on R directly, but I believe this can only be done on 2D or on surfaces of 3D shapes. I cannot add sliding landmarks in Amira, sadly. 

Does anyone have an idea of a software that would allow me to do this? Basically, either skeletonize a 3D shape and define sliding landmarks, or import the skeletonized shape (a graph, basically) and add the landmarks on that. Or even better, is there a way to do this using geomorph?

Many thanks,
Marcela

parts:
Hi Marcela,

You mean that you don’t have any more the 3D surfaces to digitize 3D semilandmarks in Amira? or you just don’t know how digitize semilandmarks in Amira? if the second option is the problem you can use the B-spline function in Amira to digitize semilandmarks as curves. Follow this path Create/Data/Bspline

You can use some functions from the Arothron package to read in R one or more files and folders with several files

I hope this helps

Best,

Miguel

Hi Marcela,

I am new to geomorph forum and am not familiar with the etiquette of discus=
sing non-geomorph related topics, so I will keep it brief:

If you need to draw arbitrary splines (open curve or closed) on a mesh (or =
a 3D volume) and sample N number of equidistant points along the spline, yo=
u can do that using 3D Slicer and SlicerMorph extension. If you only have t=
he skeletonized curves (not the original data), you might be able convert t=
hem to splines with a few lines of python code in Slicer. It depends on wha=
t format your data is currently  in. Feel free to contact me off the list.

You can do the sliding at the time of GPA.
